audit.whatIsWrong: The entry attributes Karma's root to her Mantra-empowered Q in four places — spikes[2] "Karma's Mantra-empowered Q (RQ) fires a root tether", its own stage label "RQ Root", wants.foe[1] "Use Mantra-empowered RQ root", mid "her Mantra-empowered RQ: the root tether pins you in place", whys[3] "cannot all-in without the RQ root setup".
audit.why: Karma's root is Focused Resolve (W). Mantra-empowered Q is Inner Flame plus a delayed cataclysm — pure damage, no root. This is the same shape of error as the Cassiopeia calibration case in the brief, where the grounding belonged to Miasma rather than the Q. It matters more here than a naming slip normally would, because Focused Resolve is a TETHER with real counterplay that the entry therefore never mentions: it roots only 'if the tether is not broken', and its range is 675. Tahm Kench's own Q reaches 900. So the correct instruction — walk out to break the tether before the root lands — is available to him and is completely absent, replaced by advice to fear an ability that does not root. The full layer already names Focused Resolve correctly in tldr, winCon and focus, so the two layers contradict each other on the central mechanic of the lane.
audit.corrected: The root is Focused Resolve (W), a 675-range tether on a flat 12s cooldown that roots only if you fail to break it. Mantra on W extends the root and heals her.
sources: champ-data/_kits/karma.json — W Focused Resolve: 'creates a tether between herself and a targeted enemy... If the tether is not broken, the enemy will be rooted', range 675, cooldown 12, flags hardCC+heal; Q Inner Flame Mantra Bonus: 'creating a cataclysm which deals damage after a short delay'

audit.whatIsWrong: early says "At level 1 Tongue Lash already out-ranges Karma's Q" and whys[0] repeats "Tongue Lash out-ranges her Q at level 1".
audit.why: Backwards. Inner Flame is 950 range; Tongue Lash is 900. Karma out-ranges Tahm Kench by 50 units, not the other way round. The entry builds the entire level-1 plan on a range advantage he does not have — 'throw it into the wave to contest CS and let her walk into the slow' assumes she must enter his threat range to poke, when in fact she can stand outside it and poke for free. What Tahm Kench actually has at level 1 is the sustain argument the very next sentence makes correctly (Thick Skin banking her chip), not a range argument.
audit.corrected: Inner Flame 950 beats Tongue Lash 900. The level-1 edge is Thick Skin sustain, not range.
sources: champ-data/_kits/karma.json — Q Inner Flame range 950; champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json — Q Tongue Lash range 900

audit.whatIsWrong: Devour is promised at levels 2 and 3 in four places: spikes[0] (stage "Lvl 2-3") "long enough to land a full Devour", early "At level 2 your stun is live... then stun and Devour", whys[1] "a Tongue Lash into Devour on level 2", whys[2] "Three stacks plus Devour at level 3".
audit.why: Devour is the ultimate and does not exist before level 6. This entry is the most aggressive version of the error I found — it does not merely mention Devour early, it builds the whole level-2 kill pattern on it ('step forward, land Tongue Lash, wait for the third stack confirmation, then stun and Devour... the Devour holds her long enough to burn a chunk of her health bar'). A player following that against a 950-range mage steps up at level 2 for a payoff that cannot happen, and eats Inner Flame for it.
audit.corrected: Before 6 the three-stack payoff is the Tongue Lash stun alone.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json — R Devour is the ultimate slot

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 plan is entirely "Abyssal Voyage": spikes[1] "Abyssal Voyage adds roam pressure Karma cannot match", mid "Abyssal Voyage threatens bot side and she has to choose between following you and losing her range advantage or staying top and letting you teleport a fight open", whys[4] "Abyssal Voyage adds global pressure she cannot answer with range alone".
audit.why: Abyssal Voyage is the pre-2021-rework ultimate and is not on the live champion — Tahm Kench has no global and cannot 'teleport a fight open'. The mid passage then tells the player to keep bluffing a threat that does not exist ('Keep using that threat even if you never pull the trigger — it keeps her nervous'), which against a competent Karma is simply a Tahm Kench standing in lane doing nothing.
audit.corrected: Level 6 is Devour, gated at three An Acquired Taste stacks — a lockdown, not a roam threat.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json — R Devour, no global ability in kit

audit.whatIsWrong: mid tells the player to "Watch the Mantra cooldown before you step up" and late to "Play around the Mantra cooldown as a global clock", but the number is never given, and Focused Resolve's cooldown is never given either.
audit.why: Mantra is 40/38/36/34s and Focused Resolve is a FLAT 12s at every rank. Those two numbers are the whole cooldown story of the lane and they point in opposite directions: the root is always coming back, so there is no waiting it out, whereas Mantra is a genuine 40-second clock worth counting. Telling a player to track 'the Mantra cooldown' without saying it is 40s gives him no way to actually do it.
audit.corrected: Mantra 40s at rank 1; Focused Resolve flat 12s at all ranks.
sources: champ-data/_kits/karma.json — R Mantra cooldown 40/38/36/34, W Focused Resolve cooldown 12

audit.whatIsWrong: Anti-heal is never mentioned, in either layer, despite this being the flagged missing interaction for the matchup.
audit.why: Mantra-empowered Focused Resolve heals Karma while it extends the root. In a lane the entry correctly frames as an attrition war between her chip damage and Thick Skin's grey-health recovery, a heal on her side of the ledger is exactly the variable that decides it — and it arrives on the same button as the root, so it is not an optional consideration.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds timing matters here; RW heals her.
sources: champ-data/_kits/karma.json — W Mantra Bonus: 'Karma strengthens the link, healing herself and extending the root duration', flags heal; _missing-interactions.json rule needs-antiheal for tahmkench vs karma

edits.before: At level 1 Tongue Lash already out-ranges Karma's Q and the slow keeps her in place long enough to start fishing for stacks — throw it into the wave to contest CS and let her walk into the slow when she steps up to poke. Her Q is her whole trade pattern at this stage: you heal most of it back through Thick Skin the moment you stand still for a couple of seconds. At level 2 your stun is live, so the moment she burns her Mantra on anything other than the E shield, step forward, land Tongue Lash, wait for the third stack confirmation, then stun and Devour — she has no dash to avoid it and the Devour holds her long enough to burn a chunk of her health bar.
edits.after: At level 1 Inner Flame actually out-ranges you, 950 to your 900, so you cannot win the poke war — your edge is that you heal most of her chip back through Thick Skin the moment you stand still for a couple of seconds. Throw Tongue Lash into the wave to contest CS and let her walk into the slow when she steps up. At level 2 your stun is live, so the moment she burns Mantra on anything but the E shield, step forward, land Tongue Lash and hold for the third stack — the stun is the whole payoff until 6, since Devour is your ultimate and is not available yet. If she tethers you with Focused Resolve, break it by walking, never by trading through it.

edits.before: The only real threat in this phase is her Mantra-empowered RQ: the root tether pins you in place and if she has it up when you commit to a stack-fishing pattern she can punish you hard. Watch the Mantra cooldown before you step up — if you see the glow on her, sit back and let the wave push. At level 6 she cannot match your global pressure; Abyssal Voyage threatens bot side and she has to choose between following you and losing her range advantage or staying top and letting you teleport a fight open. Keep using that threat even if you never pull the trigger — it keeps her nervous and shuts down her roam.
edits.after: The only real threat in this phase is Focused Resolve: the 675-range tether roots you only if you fail to break it, so the instant it lands walk straight away from her rather than trading through it. Watch Mantra, a 40s clock at rank 1 — if you see the glow, sit back and let the wave push, because Mantra on W both extends the root and heals her. At level 6 Devour comes online, but it needs three An Acquired Taste stacks on her before you can cast it at all, so the stun still has to land first. Her E gives move speed, not a dash, so once she is held she stays held.

edits.before: Karma's Mantra-empowered Q (RQ) fires a root tether — this is her biggest threat window, the one moment she can lock you in place and call for roam help while you have no stacks.
edits.after: Karma's Mantra-empowered W (RW) extends her root and heals her — her biggest threat window, and the tether breaks if you walk out of its 675 range before it completes.

edits.before: Three An Acquired Taste stacks into Tongue Lash stun lets you lock Karma in place long enough to land a full Devour — she has no mobility to escape once the stun lands.
edits.after: Three An Acquired Taste stacks make the Tongue Lash stun live — that alone is the level-3 payoff, since Devour is your ultimate. She has no dash to escape once the stun lands.

edits.before: Abyssal Voyage adds roam pressure Karma cannot match; if she mirrors your roam, her Q poke and RQ tether lose their home base where range is the advantage.
edits.after: Devour comes online, but only fires at three An Acquired Taste stacks; against a 950-range Inner Flame you have to earn those stacks before the ultimate means anything.

edits.before: Tongue Lash out-ranges her Q at level 1 and the slow lets you fish for stacks safely — neither of you can kill the other yet, but you set the pace of the lane.
edits.after: Inner Flame out-ranges Tongue Lash 950 to 900, so she sets the poke pace — but Thick Skin banks it back, and neither of you can kill the other yet.

edits.before: Three stacks plus Devour at level 3 is a full kill-threat combo she cannot disengage from; her Mantra E gives move speed, not a flash, so once the stun lands she is held.
edits.after: Three stacks makes the Tongue Lash stun live at level 3 — Devour is not up until 6; her Mantra E gives move speed, not a flash, so once the stun lands she is held.

edits.before: Abyssal Voyage adds global pressure she cannot answer with range alone — she has to respect a roam threat that removes her safe-haven entirely.
edits.after: Devour arrives but is gated behind three An Acquired Taste stacks — against a 950-range poke mage, landing those stacks is the whole problem at 6.

edits.before: Use Mantra-empowered RQ root to lock him in place and deny Tongue Lash stack fishing
edits.after: Land Focused Resolve (W) and hold the tether to root him out of Tongue Lash stack fishing

edits.before: Maintain range and use E move-speed to stay outside Tongue Lash range so An Acquired Taste stacks never reach three
edits.after: Poke from Inner Flame's 950 range and use E move speed to stay off his 900 Q so his stacks never reach three

notes: Karma is the clearest example in my slice of the two layers disagreeing on mechanics rather than wording: CHAMP_FULL.tahmkench.karma correctly identifies Focused Resolve as the ability to track in tldr, winCon, enemyWin and focus, while MC_CONTENT_EXTRA attributes the root to Mantra-Q in four places. Whichever generator produced the content layer had the wrong ability slot; the full layer is the trustworthy one here and could be used to cross-check the rest. Also note Karma's Mantra is available at level 1 without a skill point, so RW root pressure exists from the first wave — earlier than this entry's staging implies. This matchup also carries the file-wide pre-6 Devour defect (40 of 71 matchups; see my jayce audit for the scripted list).
